Interface ConnectionFactory

Functional Interface:
This is a functional interface and can therefore be used as the assignment target for a lambda expression or method reference.
@FunctionalInterface public interface ConnectionFactory
Factory for acquiring and releasing JDBC connections.

Implementations control the connection lifecycle — pooling, caching, per-thread reuse, or direct creation. The contract is simple:

  1. acquire() returns a usable connection
  2. release(Connection) returns it to the pool / closes it

The SqlSession class enforces the try/finally pattern automatically: 

try (SqlSession session = SqlSession.from(factory)) {
    session.sql()
        .select("SELECT NAME FROM CUST WHERE ID = ?")
        .param(custId)
        .into(rec, "WS-NAME")
        .execute();
    session.commit();
}
// connection released automatically

Built-in implementations:

  • simple(String, String, String) — DriverManager, no pooling
  • jdbc(DataSource) — delegates to a DataSource (use with HikariCP, etc.)
  • cached(ConnectionFactory, int) — simple internal pool

    • acquire

      Connection acquire()
      Acquire a connection ready for use.

    • release

      default void release(Connection connection)
      Release a connection back to the pool or close it. Default: close.

    • cached

      default ConnectionFactory cached(boolean enabled)
      Enable or disable connection caching on this factory. 
      // Wrap with caching (pool of 10):
ConnectionFactory.postgres(...).cached(true)

// Explicitly no caching (new connection each time):
ConnectionFactory.h2("mem:test").cached(false)

// SQLite in-memory REQUIRES caching (DB is per-connection):
ConnectionFactory.sqlite(":memory:").cached(true)
      Parameters:
      enabled - true = wrap in a connection pool; false = return this unchanged
      Returns:
      the same factory (if false) or a cached wrapper (if true)

    • cached

      default ConnectionFactory cached(boolean enabled, int poolSize)
      Enable caching with explicit pool size.

    • jdbc

      static ConnectionFactory jdbc(String url, String user, String password)
      Standard JDBC connection factory — works with any database that has a JDBC driver. This is the primary entry point for PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, Oracle, DB2, etc.

      Explicit commit is the default (autoCommit=false), matching COBOL transactional semantics. Chain .cached(true) if you want connection reuse. 

      // PostgreSQL
ConnectionFactory.jdbc("jdbc:postgresql://db:5432/orders", "user", "pass").cached(true)

// MySQL / MariaDB
ConnectionFactory.jdbc("jdbc:mysql://db:3306/orders", "user", "pass").cached(true)

// Oracle
ConnectionFactory.jdbc("jdbc:oracle:thin:@//db:1521/ORCL", "user", "pass").cached(true)

// DB2
ConnectionFactory.jdbc("jdbc:db2://db:50000/ORDERS", "user", "pass").cached(true)

// Any JDBC URL — just put the driver on the classpath
ConnectionFactory.jdbc(url, user, pass).cached(true)

    • jdbc

      static ConnectionFactory jdbc(DataSource ds)
      JDBC factory backed by a javax.sql.DataSource (HikariCP, Tomcat JDBC, etc.). Use when the DataSource handles pooling externally.

    • h2InMemory

      static ConnectionFactory h2InMemory(String name)
      H2 in-memory database — data exists only for the lifetime of the JVM. Connection is cached by default because H2 in-memory DBs require at least one live connection to persist.

      For file-based H2, use the standard JDBC API: ConnectionFactory.jdbc("jdbc:h2:./data/myapp", "", "") 

      ConnectionFactory.h2InMemory("testdb")   // explicit: this is ephemeral

    • sqliteInMemory

      static ConnectionFactory sqliteInMemory()
      SQLite in-memory database — data exists only for the lifetime of the connection. Automatically cached because SQLite in-memory DBs are per-connection.

      For file-based SQLite, use the standard JDBC API: ConnectionFactory.jdbc("jdbc:sqlite:/data/app.db", null, null) 

      ConnectionFactory.sqliteInMemory()       // explicit: this is ephemeral
